findings.message: Reviewed the current CONTRACT.md, workflow.py, and test_workflow.py. No blocking workflow defect found. Distinct requester/approver enforcement, authorized revocation, terminal denied/revoked states, durable resource allowlist, strict TTL/clock validation, and read-only check precedence (unknown request, resource, actor, expiry, approval) match the lab contract. Approval preserves the original expiry and reason.

workflow.py uses parameterized SQL and a separate connection per operation. BEGIN IMMEDIATE precedes mutation state reads and clock evaluation; each successful mutation inserts exactly one audit event before the same transaction commits. The exception path rolls back both. No override or real access-grant path was found.

Executed python3 -B -m unittest -v: all 21 tests passed, including CLI exit codes, import side effects, persistence, SQL payloads, threaded single-winner approval, and trigger-injected audit failure rollback for request/approve/deny/revoke. Additional temporary-directory checks passed for cross-process approval/approval and approval/denial races and rejection at expiry with a writer lock held when approval was launched. No code or QA tests were modified.

Approval is limited to the explicitly documented local laboratory: actors are trusted strings at the OS-user boundary, SQLite audit is ordinary transactional storage writable by its owner, and there is no authentication, credential handling, external service, network call, or actual grant integration. This is not production PAM approval.
